hints: Focus on how much gas each type of reaction makes, carbonates make only $\text{CO}_2$ but nitrates make $\text{NO}_2$ plus $\text{O}_2$.
Write the two balanced equations and notice that 1 mol of carbonate gives 1 mol of gas, while 1 mol of nitrate gives 2.5 mol of gas.
Combine moles of starting solid in 1.0 g (moles = mass / $M_r$) with moles of gas per mole to find which gives most gas overall.
walkthrough:
**Write the decomposition equations**

Think of it simply, heat drives off the non-metal part as gas and leaves the metal oxide behind.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{MCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MO} + \text{CO}_2$$
$$2\text{M}(\text{NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Count gas moles per mole of solid**

A carbonate gives just 1 mole of gas per mole. A nitrate gives much more gas per mole.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$1 \text{ mol MCO}_3 \rightarrow 1 \text{ mol gas}$$
$$1 \text{ mol M(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2 + 0.5 = 2.5 \text{ mol gas}$$

**Find moles in 1.0 g of each solid**

We all start with the same mass, so the lighter solid gives more starting moles. Use moles = mass / $M_r$.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$M_r(\text{CaCO}_3) = 100.1, \quad M_r(\text{Ca}(\text{NO}_3)_2) = 164.1$$
$$M_r(\text{SrCO}_3) = 147.6, \quad M_r(\text{Sr}(\text{NO}_3)_2) = 211.6$$

**Calculate gas moles and pick the largest**

Multiply starting moles by gas per mole. Volume at room conditions is directly proportional to moles of gas.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{A: } \frac{1.0}{100.1} \times 1 = 0.0100 \text{ mol}$$
$$\text{B: } \frac{1.0}{164.1} \times 2.5 = 0.0152 \text{ mol}$$
$$\text{C: } \frac{1.0}{147.6} \times 1 = 0.0068 \text{ mol}$$
$$\text{D: } \frac{1.0}{211.6} \times 2.5 = 0.0118 \text{ mol}$$

options.A: Calcium carbonate is light ($M_r$ about 100) so 1.0 g is about 0.01 mol, but it gives only 1 mol $\text{CO}_2$ per mole. That gives about 0.01 mol gas, less than the best nitrate which benefits from 2.5 mol gas per mole.
options.B: Calcium nitrate combines two advantages. It is the lighter nitrate ($M_r$ about 164) so 1.0 g gives more moles than strontium nitrate, and as a nitrate it gives 2.5 mol gas ($2\text{NO}_2 + 0.5\text{O}_2$) per mole. This gives about 0.015 mol gas, the largest volume.
options.C: Strontium carbonate is heavier ($M_r$ about 148) and gives only 1 mol $\text{CO}_2$ per mole. So 1.0 g gives only about 0.0068 mol gas, the smallest of the four.
options.D: Strontium nitrate does give 2.5 mol gas per mole, but it is very heavy ($M_r$ about 212). So 1.0 g contains very few moles, giving about 0.0118 mol gas, which is beaten by the lighter calcium nitrate.
